messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The failing test `testIterateJDOM()` in `AliasedNamespaceIterationTest` calls `doTestIterate(DocumentContainer.MODEL_JDOM)`, which in turn verifies XPath pointer iteration over elements using the "JDOM" model. The test constructs a JXPathContext via `createContext(model)` that internally creates a DocumentContainer from a given model and XML resource. Namespaces are registered on the context with prefix "a" bound to the namespace URI "ns".

The current bug report indicates a problem in `JXPathContext.iteratePointers(String xpath)` when there are multiple prefixes mapped to the same namespace URI. The report gives an example where two elements share the same namespace URI but have different prefixes ("a" and "b"). When calling `iteratePointers()`, only the first element is returned multiple times, and the second element is ignored. This suggests that prefix aliasing is not correctly handled during pointer iteration.

The `iteratePointers()` method is abstract in `JXPathContext`, so the actual fault likely lies in the implementation used with the JDOM model. The test expects that iterator to return pointers for different elements even if they have different prefixes but share the same namespace URI. Failure symptoms in the report indicate that the prefix-to-namespace mappings are not being properly resolved or disambiguated during iteration, causing duplicate nodes to be returned for the first prefix and missing nodes for other prefixes sharing the same URI.

Thus, the root cause stems from how the namespace prefix aliasing is handled in the evaluation logic behind `iteratePointers()`. It does not correctly maintain distinct namespace prefix mappings when different prefixes refer to the same namespace URI, resulting in erroneous pointer iteration behavior with duplicate results and omitted elements.

No recent bug reports are relevant to this namespace aliasing or pointer iteration issue.

In summary, the failure occurs because `JXPathContext.iteratePointers()` and its underlying model implementations do not correctly handle multiple prefixes bound to the same namespace URI, causing incorrect iteration results as seen in the test failure and described in the current bug report.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
